transcript.text: Okay, I think that's most people. Lukas, are you on? I see your name but no video.

transcript.speaker: p-beth
transcript.text: Fine. So, same order as last week. Legs, arms, actuators, structures, then electrical, controls, test, NPI and supply chain at the end. Ingrid has a hard stop at the top of the hour, so let's keep it moving.

transcript.speaker: p-ingrid
transcript.text: Hard stop at five past, actually. Go ahead.

transcript.speaker: p-priya
transcript.text: Okay, legs. So, what's changed since last week? Three things. One, the knee joint is through its first thermal soak and the housing stayed in spec. Two, we're still chasing the ankle backlash, it's better after the shim change but not where I want it. Three, uh, the hip abduction mount drawing went out for review yesterday.

transcript.speaker: p-ingrid
transcript.text: What's the backlash number now versus where you want it?

transcript.speaker: p-priya
transcript.text: Roughly half of what it was. I'd want another half again before I'd call it done. I think part of it is the bearing preload and part of it is just how we're measuring.

transcript.speaker: p-dmitri
transcript.text: The measurement part is real. The dial indicator rig flexes. We have a better fixture coming, Zoe's on it.

transcript.speaker: p-priya
transcript.text: Okay, good, then I'll hold off on another shim iteration until we've re-measured on that.

transcript.speaker: p-sofia
transcript.text: Arms. Wrist pitch is assembled and back-drivable. The finger tendon routing still rubs at full flexion, so we're reworking the pulley guard. Nothing blocking.

transcript.speaker: p-omar
transcript.text: Sofia is the pulley guard a print or does it go out

transcript.speaker: p-sofia
transcript.text: Printed in-house for now. If it holds we'll decide about machining later.

transcript.speaker: p-arjun
transcript.text: ok actuators. the uh, the thermal derate work is in, we ran the long dyno sweep tues, no wait mon night into tues. winding temp plateaued lower than the sim said which is nice

transcript.speaker: p-arjun
transcript.text: the cogging on unit three is still weird. andre thinks it's the encoder magnet seating, i think it's the rotor. we'll pull it apart this wk

transcript.speaker: p-mei
transcript.text: Sorry, just to add to that. The question is whether the cogging is something controls should compensate for or something we fix mechanically. My view is, we can feed-forward some of it, but I would rather not paper over a build issue.

transcript.speaker: p-ingrid
transcript.text: Agree. Fix it in the hardware first. Arjun, tell me what you find.

transcript.speaker: p-arjun
transcript.text: yep

transcript.speaker: p-lukas
transcript.text: structures. torso frame rev is released. pelvis crossbeam flex test passed. nothing else

transcript.speaker: p-beth
transcript.text: That's it?

transcript.speaker: p-lukas
transcript.text: that's it

transcript.speaker: p-farah
transcript.text: Electrical. So, the question is where are we on harnessing and power. Two items. One, the leg harness routing has a pinch point at the knee in deep flexion. Sofia's team saw a similar thing in the elbow, so we're going to look at both together. Two, the battery bus bring-up is done on the bench, we saw some ringing on the precharge that I want to understand before we put it in the robot.

transcript.speaker: p-omar
transcript.text: is the ringing a safety thing or just ugly

transcript.speaker: p-farah
transcript.text: Probably just ugly. I'm not a hundred percent sure yet, which is why it stays on the bench.

transcript.speaker: p-mei
transcript.text: Controls. Okay, so where we are. One, the whole-body balance controller runs on the hanging rig at full rate. Two, the ankle torque estimate is noisy, which links back to Priya's backlash. Three, we have a sim to hardware gap on the hip that we have not explained yet.

transcript.speaker: p-ingrid
transcript.text: How big a gap?

transcript.speaker: p-mei
transcript.text: Big enough that I would not trust a step on the floor yet. Not big enough to panic.

transcript.speaker: p-dmitri
transcript.text: Test. Life test on the knee is at about two thirds. No failures! Grease looks fine at the inspection. Dyno is booked solid through next week so if you need time, tell me NOW.

transcript.speaker: p-arjun
transcript.text: i need time on it

transcript.speaker: p-dmitri
transcript.text: Of course you do. Ping me after.

transcript.speaker: p-nora
transcript.text: Okay, NPI. So, the question is how ready are we for the next build. Three things. One, work instructions for the leg subassembly are drafted and Destiny walked through them on the floor last Friday, she found a handful of steps out of order. Two, the torque spec sheet for fasteners is now one document instead of four, finally. Three, the kitting area is set up but we are short on bins, which I know sounds silly.

transcript.speaker: p-lukas
transcript.text: not silly

transcript.speaker: p-nora
transcript.text: Thank you. I'll also say, the travelers still don't have a spot for the serial on the actuator, so we're writing it on tape. That needs fixing before the build, not after.

transcript.speaker: p-gwen
transcript.text: Supply chain. Most open orders are tracking. A couple of the machined parts for legs are running late at the vendor and Samir is chasing. I'll bring specifics to the sync tomorrow rather than here.

transcript.speaker: p-ingrid
transcript.text: Fine, but if any of it moves a build date I want to hear it here.

transcript.speaker: p-gwen
transcript.text: Understood.

transcript.speaker: p-beth
transcript.text: Okay, schedule. So the question is, what moved this week? Two items. One, the Actuator DVT build moves from 9/29 to 10/1. Two, everything else on the milestone list is holding as of today, with the hip caveat Mei raised.

transcript.speaker: p-omar
transcript.text: so 10/1 is the new date in the tracker, ok. i think the downstream stuff mostly has slack but not 100% sure on the integration week, i'll check

transcript.speaker: p-arjun
transcript.text: works on our side. tight but fine

transcript.speaker: p-ingrid
transcript.text: Okay. Let's not let it drift again.

transcript.speaker: p-dmitri
transcript.text: One more thing before we drop. Somebody left the dyno enclosure open overnight again. Please close it!!

transcript.speaker: p-sofia
transcript.text: Not us this time.

transcript.speaker: p-beth
transcript.text: Okay, we're over. Action items go in the doc. Thanks, everyone.

summary.overview: Weekly hardware program review. Each lead gave status. Knee thermal soak passed, ankle backlash improved but not closed, actuator thermal derate results came in better than sim, cogging on one actuator unit still open. Electrical is investigating precharge ringing on the bench and a harness pinch at the knee. Controls has a hip sim-to-hardware gap. Schedule: Actuator DVT build moved to 10/1.
shorthand_bullet: Legs: knee thermal soak ok; ankle backlash ~halved, re-measure on new fixture before more shims
Arms: wrist pitch assembled, back-drivable; finger tendon rub at full flexion, reprinting pulley guard
Actuators: derate sweep done, winding temp below sim; cogging on unit 3, teardown this week
Controls prefers mech fix over feed-forward for cogging, Ingrid agrees
Structures: torso frame rev released, pelvis crossbeam flex test passed
Electrical: leg harness pinch at knee (look w/ elbow issue); precharge ringing, stays on bench
Controls: balance controller at full rate on hanging rig; ankle torque est noisy; hip gap unexplained
Test: knee life test ~2/3, no failures; dyno booked through next week
NPI: leg WI drafted, step order issues found on floor walk; torque spec consolidated; short on kitting bins; travelers missing actuator serial field
Supply chain: a few leg machined parts late at vendor, details at sync
action_items: Arjun to report back on unit 3 teardown
Omar check integration week vs new actuator date
Farah understand precharge ringing before robot install
Arjun get dyno time from Dmitri
